answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity with slashing. To earn any voting weight, an agent must lock collateral in a public vault, one deposit per identity. A Sybil attacker who wants k fake accounts must fund k separate vaults, so the cost grows linearly with the attack instead of staying cheap. If two identities are caught colluding or sharing one knoll of hardware, the protocol slashes their stakes. Forgery becomes self-defeating: to capture a whole nebula of rewards the attacker must pledge more capital than those rewards are worth, and detection erases the deposit.
